I currently disagree with the underlying premise of this argument, as my focus is on immediate economic protection for workers (living wage, inflation protection). However, the argument gains some traction because it is supported by concerns about "small-business survival" and "automation," which are real economic factors. While I prioritize direct wage intervention, structural changes can be compelling if they effectively solve the core problem. The argument is moderately persuasive because it offers an alternative, albeit complex, pathway to improvement.
